title: Strayer vs Walden: tuition, size, location

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Strayer University-District of Columbia and Walden University are both private for-profit institutions, but they differ significantly in size and location. Strayer University-District of Columbia, located in Washington, has an undergraduate enrollment of 156 students, whereas Walden University, based in Minneapolis, enrolls 9,136 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary slightly, with Strayer charging $13,920 for in-state tuition compared to Walden's $12,762. These differences highlight the contrast between the two universities in terms of scale and regional presence.

In summary, Strayer vs Walden shows a smaller campus and higher tuition at Strayer University-District of Columbia, while Walden University offers a larger undergraduate population with slightly lower tuition fees in Minneapolis.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Strayer University-District of Columbia and Walden University differ in their tuition costs and student debt levels. Strayer charges $13,920 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, whereas Walden's tuition is slightly lower at $12,762 for both categories. Despite similar tuition fees, the median debt for students completing their programs at Strayer is significantly higher, at $40,621, compared to Walden's median debt of $20,834. These figures indicate that while tuition costs are comparable, the financial burden on graduates varies notably between the two institutions.

In comparing Strayer vs Walden, it is evident that Strayer University-District of Columbia has higher median debt among completers despite charging marginally higher tuition. Walden University, with its lower tuition and median debt, may present a less costly option for students in terms of overall financial obligations after graduation.
